_README: Every human judgement about this ROM lives in this file; the
generated listings are disposable, so renaming is free.
What to do next, roughly in order:
Read the coverage it reports. Low coverage is normal at
first and is the number you are trying to move.
2. Every unresolved indirect jump it reports is a hole. Add the
target to `entries`, or the pointer pair to `ram_vectors` if
the handler is installed into RAM.
Finds the sound code and the tables feeding it.
4. Name things in `labels` as soon as you know what they are.
See docs/method.md for the working order and docs/pitfalls.md for
the traps that each cost real time.

comments.f8:FEA8: NMI: WSYNC, then JMP ($65). Each handler ends in DliNext, which loads the next handler's address from a 9-entry RAM table ($253C, index $5E) -- a scene picks its band colours by poking that table. The last handler (Dli_Bottom) sets FrameDone for WaitFrame. No bank switch in any interrupt (live: runs/xb/xt1/banks.txt).
comments.f8:FD2E: Append one 4-byte header [lo, palette/width, hi, x] to zone $48's list through that zone's fill pointer ($24E0,zone*2), then a zero terminator. 12 lists of 128 bytes at $1800-$1DFF. No cap test.
comments.f8:FCB2: Place an object: zone = RowToZone[y >> 4], fine = y & 15; a misaligned object takes one more zone and starts fine pages lower; each further zone steps the high byte by $10. One column, one palette, one width for the whole figure (friends are 48 lines = 3 zones). No holey DMA: the art carries blank pages.
comments.f8:FCFC: Start of a frame's drawing: the fill pointers go back to the values saved after the scene's fixed background was laid (SaveListHeads), so only the moving objects are redrawn.
comments.f8:F8C4: Actor animation script: [frames to hold, gfx lo, dx, dy] per step (no dx/dy if $2360 bit 7). A zero hold is an escape: next byte / 2 selects sound, loop (count in $23C0, 16-bit target), set state, score popup, set loop count, move.
comments.f8:E50A: The only bank switch: once when a scene is loaded, in vblank (raster 255, live). SceneBank = 0,3,2,4,3,6,1,5,4,2,0 for scenes 0-10 (file bank = value + 1).
comments.f8:D772: Each scene is its own routine (table SceneHandlers): it draws the fixed background from record streams, then loops calling that scene's actor routines once a frame until no friend is left.
